current: Coding and synthesis were performed by the six-member review panel described in Section 2.3.1. For each full text, the panel executed a fixed review template
replacement: Coding and synthesis followed the six-role review procedure described in Section 2.3.1. For each full text, a fixed review template was executed. The first role verified the completeness of the full text and the bibliographic identity of the record and applied the eligibility and quality gates. The second role coded consent representation and trust modelling. The third role coded identity, authority and multi-party authorisation. The fourth role coded policy, temporal and lifecycle enforcement. The fifth role coded formal assurance and empirical validation. The chair issued the final decision and the gap-impact verdict. Where a role disagreed with the final decision, the dissent was recorded in the register against the study together with the reason, and the decision of the chair stood subject to the author's ratification. A dissent was never removed from the log, so that the boundary cases remain visible in the sensitivity analysis. For full texts whose abstract already suggested a positive coding on a contested dimension, the tests that would decide that coding were pre-registered in the decision log before the full text was read, so that the outcome could not be adjusted after reading. The matrix of T1 to T7 and Req1 to Req7 values was re-derived from the register at every checkpoint, and the synthesis in Section 2.5 is based on the values held in the register at decision D-166.
